nodes.label: Firebase + PWA Integration Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: 10-task, checkbox-tracked implementation plan wiring real Firebase Auth + Firestore into the Delbert boarding-house app (login, dashboard, chats, friends, requests, reports, accounts), converting it to an installable mobile-responsive PWA, and enforcing 24h post/report expiry plus 4h message expiry with matching Firestore security rules. Explicitly written for agentic execution via superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans, task-by-task with tsc/build verification and commits per task.

nodes.label: Client-side Expiry Filter (moving now-tick)
nodes.rationale: Every read query (posts, messages) applies `where('expiresAt', '>', now)` in addition to relying on Firestore TTL. Crucially the `now` bound is a state value (`nowTick`) refreshed every 60s via setInterval, not captured once at mount — because Firestore's realtime listener does not re-evaluate an inequality against a moving 'now', so a document crossing its expiresAt in an open tab would otherwise keep matching the original snapshot's cutoff and linger on screen until the slow TTL sweep actually deletes it. This is the mechanism that makes visible expiry exact regardless of TTL sweep timing, per spec ruling R6.

nodes.label: Conversations participantIds Immutability
nodes.rationale: firestore.rules forbids any update to a conversation document that changes its participantIds array after creation. Without this, either participant could rewrite participantIds to add a third party or drop the other person, retroactively exposing or locking someone out of the entire prior message history — because the messages subcollection's own rules trust the parent conversation document's *current* participantIds to decide read/write access.

nodes.label: profileRef Memoization Fix
nodes.rationale: In lib/auth-context.tsx, `doc(db, 'users', firebaseUser.uid)` is wrapped in `useMemo(..., [firebaseUser?.uid])` rather than called bare, because Firestore's doc() returns a fresh DocumentReference with no stable identity on every call. Without memoization, useDocument's `[ref]`-keyed effect would see a 'changed' ref on every render — including the re-renders its own onSnapshot callback triggers via setData — producing an infinite unsubscribe/resubscribe loop for as long as anyone is logged in, not just a wasted render.

nodes.label: Firestore Query/DocumentReference Instability Pattern
nodes.rationale: Global Constraint stated up front: Firestore JS SDK query() and doc() objects are not stable across renders, so every call site feeding useCollection/useDocument in this plan wraps the query/doc construction in useMemo keyed on the primitive values it depends on (never the auth/profile object itself). Applies uniformly to postsQuery, conversationsQuery, messagesQuery, usersQuery, outgoing/incomingQuery, and profileRef — stated once as a rule that every task must follow rather than re-derived per task.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled PWA Shell (manifest + minimal service worker)
nodes.rationale: PWA support is a hand-rolled web app manifest plus a minimal service worker rather than the `next-pwa` package, because next-pwa is webpack-only and this project builds with Turbopack. The service worker itself uses a network-first fetch strategy (falling back to the cached app shell only when the network fails) so residents always see live posts/messages when online — explicitly scoped to app-shell caching only, no push notifications or background sync, per the spec's Out of Scope ruling.

nodes.label: Honesty Principle: Don't Invent Data
nodes.rationale: Explicitly named in the plan's Task 4 note as 'a direct application of the Honesty principle carried over from this session's earlier graphify pass: don't invent data.' Applied concretely by dropping RightRail's fabricated 'residents online' pulse card rather than keeping fake numbers (the data model has no presence beyond a boolean), and by flagging friendRequests' raw fromUid display in RequestsView as a known rough edge rather than silently faking a resolved display name. Also underlies the decision to leave NotificationPopover's mock content clearly out of scope rather than partially wiring it to real data.
